questions.explanation: At work 'invallen' means to stand in for a colleague and cover their shift.

questions.prompt: Hoe zeg je 'Are you coming along?'
questions.explanation: 'Meegaan' = to come along; the separable verb splits: 'Ga je mee?'
It is 'de afspraak' (the appointment); 'afspraak' is a de-woord.
With 'we' the verb 'gaan' stays 'gaan': 'Wat gaan we ... doen?' The infinitive 'doen' goes to the end.

questions.prompt: Sorry, ik kan vrijdag niet {{1}}, want ik moet werken. (meegaan)
questions.explanation: After the modal verb 'kan', the separable verb stays together as an infinitive at the end: 'meegaan'.

questions.prompt: Vrijdag ben ik {{1}}, dan hoef ik niet te werken. (free / off)
questions.explanation: 'Vrij' means free or off work; 'ik ben vrij' = I have the day off.

questions.prompt: Kun je vrijdag voor mij ________? Ik kan niet komen. (een dienst overnemen)
questions.explanation: 'Invallen' = to cover the shift, to stand in for someone who cannot come.

questions.prompt: Vul in om beleefd 'nee' te zeggen: 'Sorry, dat komt niet ________.'
questions.explanation: 'Dat komt niet uit' is a polite way to say no: it isn't convenient for me.
